_comment: Natural-key + FK + resolve config for bin/db-merge.py, generated 2026-09-10 from the natural-key inventory (123 tables, 13 live databases; jc.db and barback.db excluded, no tables).

checklists.note: No updated/created columns exist (inventory: 'table has NO timestamp column'), so no resolve rule applies -- a genuine field conflict here has no tiebreaker and surfaces as a plain conflict. Two triggers (checklists_protect_delete, checklists_protect_identity) RAISE on delete/rename of a protected row -- apply drops/recreates triggers around the merge. 13/16 rows have empty source, so the partial UNIQUE(source) gives no help.

checklist_items.note: (checklist_id, text) verified unique on both copies 2026-09-10. section and sort_order are NOT identity: the Mac re-sectioned three lists after the fork, and keying on section made every moved item read as a delete plus an add (72 false conflicts in the first dry run). They merge three-way like any other column; a list rearranged on both sides is a real conflict, settled with --prefer. (checklist_id, sort_order) COLLIDES, never use position as identity. checked has no timestamp; resolve:max means a tick wins over an untick.

holding.note: Inventory also wants first_seen resolved by MIN, but the merge-keys vocabulary only defines newest/max; first_seen is left as default conflict (judgment call -- flag for human review if it ever actually diverges).

earnings_scheduled_shifts.note: calendar_event_id is a convention-only external Google Calendar id (no FK) -- a strong secondary match key if the primary ever needs a fallback.

evidence.note: Identity is really the quote text; a re-scrape with reworded quote text will duplicate rather than conflict (accepted content-hash cost).

activities.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

activity_opinions.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

application_process_steps.note: (application_id, step_order) is also unique today, but label survives a reorder -- prefer it.

applications.note: Root of the whole db -- every child NK resolves through it.

company_research.note: subcategory is NULL on some rows; COALESCE it when matching -- SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in the declared UNIQUE index so it would not actually stop a dup there.

expenses.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

flights.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

glossary.note: known is a per-machine read flag; inventory calls for OR/take-either semantics -- resolve:max approximates that (judgment call).

housing.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

interview_qa.note: source_template_id is a SELF-referential surrogate -- remap it in a second pass after this table's own id map exists. Template rows carry application_id NULL + is_template=1, hence the key is really (COALESCE(app NK,'template'), question).

members.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

resume_notes.note: note is the body, so an edit reads as a new row rather than a conflict (accepted content-hash cost). Only 11 rows -- flag for human review.

resumes.note: file_path is the real identity -- it names a file on disk, globally unique.

transportation.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

trips.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover, 0 rows on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

owed.note: 11/66 rows have NULL incurred -- COALESCE it. src embeds trips.db surrogate ids (machine-specific) and is re-derived by the finances module after trips.db merges, so it and src_amount are excluded from comparison. Never overwrite amount from src_amount -- their divergence IS Sam's manual-override flag.

payment.note: ext_id and msg_id are convention-only external ids (no FK). All 17 rows currently have a non-empty ext_id; inventory's documented fallback for a future NULL ext_id row is (person, amount, received), not currently implemented in this key.

saved_searches.note: (query, sites) is not UNIQUE in the schema: two saves of the same query and sites read as one key to the merge. last_run/seeded_at are job clocks, resolve:max.

candidate_constraints.note: status/note are the conflict fields, with no clock to break a tie -- left as default conflict.

candidates.note: Second-level root: most other NKs resolve through it. No timestamp column, so a genuine field conflict here has no tiebreaker.

decisions.note: verdict_candidate_id and project_id are CONVENTION-ONLY (no declared FK, so foreign_key_check will never catch a stale pointer) -- remap both in the second pass after candidates/projects merge.

order_emails.note: message_id is a Gmail message id -- perfect natural key.

orders.note: JUDGMENT CALL: inventory's table row proposes (vendor, order_number, ordered_on), but its own note flags 2 live rows with empty order_number where 'vendor alone is doing the work' and explicitly recommends 'include ordered_on and item' -- added item to the key on that basis. ship_status and eta have no resolve rule of their own (they are not clocks); inventory says they should follow whichever side has the newer updated -- the vocabulary has no cross-column resolve, so this is left as a note rather than encoded; the tool will otherwise report ship_status/eta as a plain conflict when they differ.

price_points.note: (candidate_id, vendor, observed_on) COLLIDES -- e.g. candidate 1 / awaytravel.com / 2026-05-15 has two rows ($295 and $206) on both sides. content-hash over price too is what actually de-dups; two same-day observations with no price difference are still indistinguishable by design.

reviews.note: (decision_id, candidate_id, url, title) COLLIDES -- four Pack Hacker rows share one URL and title (1 positive + 3 negative takeaways); only takeaway separates them, which is exactly why content-hash rather than keyed.

specs.note: (candidate_id, key) COLLIDES: 2 dup groups on both sides (candidate 41 'Lock', candidate 46 'Interior', each a terse early row plus a later sourced/verbatim row). content-hash over (candidate, key, value) de-dups but will double any row whose value was edited on one machine -- hand Sam the list of candidates whose key repeats so he can collapse them.

transaction_memos.note: recorded_at alone COLLIDES (2 memos on 2026-08-31) -- it is a DATE, not a timestamp. Prefer ynab_transaction_id as the match key when it is set (5/9 rows have it NULL and fall back to the content hash); ynab_transaction_id is convention-only (no FK, not a vault table) so it is informational only, not encoded as fk.

stocks.note: latest_analysis_id is a declared surrogate FK -- remap in the second pass, or recompute from the newest run_date. Inventory also wants first_analyzed resolved by MIN and the latest_* fields to follow whichever analysis is newest; the vocabulary has no min rule or cross-column follow, so first_analyzed is left as default conflict (judgment call) and latest_* fields are not separately resolved.

briefing_day.note: Regenerable weather cache. Take ours and re-run the generator rather than merging rows.

tasks.note: Best-behaved table in the vault: 0 NULL/empty task_key, 0 dups on either side. status has no resolve rule of its own; inventory says it should follow the newer updated side -- left as a note, not encoded, since the vocabulary has no cross-column resolve. cal_event_id/cal_calendar_id are convention-only external Google Calendar ids (no FK), per-event not per-machine, and survive the merge unchanged.

activities.note: (trip_id, name) COLLIDES -- 'Leave home base' appears twice per trip on trips 60 and 61; adding the schedule clears it, but rescheduling on one machine reads as a new row. score/true_score are recomputed fields -- inventory says prefer the newer side wholesale, but there is no resolve rule for a non-clock numeric column in this vocabulary, so they are left as default conflict (judgment call). cal_event_id/cal_event_ids are external Google ids.

guest_codes.note: code alone COLLIDES (7447 is both a denied 'Victor' and an approved 'Victor Lin') and name alone COLLIDES ('Sam Rivera' denied then approved) -- created_at is what actually separates rows. Trigger guest_codes_approved_needs_slug RAISEs on an approved row with no contact_slug; insert with that invariant satisfied or drop/recreate the trigger around the merge.

guest_gate_stats.note: Singleton row (id=1) of brute-force-gate counters -- no business identity. Machine-local security state; take the live side rather than merging.

housing.note: SCHEMA DIFF: live has wifi_ssid/wifi_pass (trips migration 023); the PC snapshot does not. Apply migration 023 to the snapshot before merging, or the tool must tolerate a missing column.

packing_ticks.note: The one genuinely cross-database dependency. list_id/item_id are checklists.db autoincrement ids with NO declared FK (migration 022 says so deliberately) -- checklists.db must be merged FIRST and its old->new id map kept, or ticks silently point at the wrong items.

trips.note: cal_event_id is an external Google Calendar id (convention-only, declared UNIQUE) -- a good cross-check. cal_status is flagged newer-wins in the inventory but the table has no updated/created timestamp to arbitrate it against -- left as default conflict (judgment call, flag for human review if it ever diverges).

map_node.note: Documented in data/CLAUDE.md as a cache, wiped and repopulated in full on every refresh. Take either side and re-run vault_map.db.refresh().

node_description.note: Derived cache; content_sig says whether the description is still valid. Union by path, newer generated_at wins, then refresh.

activities.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

activity_opinions.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

checklist_run_item.note: (run_id, sort_order) is also unique but position is fragile; the snapshot columns make the row self-describing. state doubles as a 0-3 count for kind='fill' rows (migration 017).

expenses.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

flights.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

housing.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

members.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

prep_day_step.note: seq is a generated plan order, stable within a prep day -- used as a tiebreak, not treated as a surrogate.

recipe_ingredients.note: (recipe_id, ingredient) is also unique today; sort_order is kept only as a tiebreak since a reorder on one machine would otherwise split rows.

recipes.note: name alone COLLIDES (15 dup groups) -- the same name exists as both a cocktail and a prep recipe. (kind, name) is clean on both sides.

storage_item.note: (section_id, text) COLLIDES: 2 dup groups on both sides -- section 58 lists 'Campari' twice (sort 64 and 70) and 'Haku Vodka' twice (14 and 37), i.e. the same bottle genuinely sits in two slots. sort_order is the only thing separating them, and a reorder on one machine changes exactly that column -- a shelf reordered on one machine will duplicate its whole section. Needs human review; consider merging this table by taking one side whole.

storage_note.note: Singleton free-text note, one row (id=1). Take the newer updated side, or concatenate the two bodies by hand.

storage_section.note: Self-referential nesting (parent_id) -- resolve parents top-down (parent_id NULL first), then remap children in a second pass.

transportation.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

trips.note: Vestigial trip-schema leftover; migration 009 (drop_vestigial_trip_tables) dropped 8 of these tables and left these 8 behind, empty on both sides. SKIP -- do not create rows here.

decisions.note: Append-only sign-off ledger; id is a uuid4 so rows from two machines never collide. seq is per-build and can tie across machines; store.current() breaks ties on decided_at.

playlists.note: Export rows are unique by file_name+grp; lists first seen by the pull have no file_name and are told apart by spotify_id. The pull runs on the active_machine only, so a spotify_id filled on one side alone is the PC's link and should win.
